It was established in 2013. The regular season started on 17 November 2017 and ended on 4 March 2018,{{cite news|title=Schedule for new season announced, ATK and Kerala Blasters FC to play first match on 17 November|url=http://www.firstpost.com/sports/isl-2017-18-schedule-for-new-season-announced-atk-and-kerala-blasters-fc-to-play-first-match-on-17-november-4070543.html|access-date=22 September 2017|work=FirstPost|date=22 September 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170922194444/http://www.firstpost.com/sports/isl-2017-18-schedule-for-new-season-announced-atk-and-kerala-blasters-fc-to-play-first-match-on-17-november-4070543.html|archive-date=22 September 2017|url-status=live}} [[2018 Indian Super League playoffs|The Playoffs]] began on 7 March 2018, concluding with [[2018 Indian Super League final|the final]] on 17 March 2018. [[ATK (football club)|ATK]] were the defending champions from the [[2016 Indian Super League|2016 season]], however they could not advance to the playoffs. [[Chennaiyin FC|Chennaiyin]] won their second Indian Super League title by defeating [[Bengaluru FC|Bengaluru]] 3–2 in the final.{{cite news|title=FSDL announces change in Hero ISL fixtures, Bengaluru to host final|url=https://www.indiansuperleague.com/press-releases/bengaluru-to-host-hero-isl-final-201718|access-date=9 March 2018|archive-date=6 July 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210706115548/https://www.indiansuperleague.com/press-releases/bengaluru-to-host-hero-isl-final-201718|url-status=live}} Two new sides joined the league as expansion teams: [[Bengaluru FC|Bengaluru]] and [[Jamshedpur FC|Jamshedpur]]. The two new clubs are the ninth and tenth teams in the league. This made it the first edition of the ISL in which there are more than eight teams participating.{{cite news|title=Indian Football Set For Exponential Growth; Indian Super League expands to 10 cities with inclusion of Bengaluru & Jamshedpur|url=http://www.indiansuperleague.com/press-releases/5566-indian-football-set-for-exponential-growth-indian-super-league-expands-to-10-cities-with-inclusion-of-bengaluru-jamshedpur|access-date=13 June 2017|work=Indian Super League|date=12 June 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170618012945/http://www.indiansuperleague.com/press-releases/5566-indian-football-set-for-exponential-growth-indian-super-league-expands-to-10-cities-with-inclusion-of-bengaluru-jamshedpur|archive-date=18 June 2017|url-status=live}}This is also the first ISL which was officially recognised by AFC as joint top division league along with [[I-League]]. As well as expanding two teams, the league also expanded two more months, being played in five months instead of three. On 25 May 2017, it was announced that bidding for new teams had ended and that the league's appointed external validator would look over the bids.{{cite news|title=Bengaluru FC submit bid as ITB submission deadline ends|url=http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/bengaluru-fc-submit-bid-as-itb-submission-deadline-ends/articleshow/58851199.cms|access-date=31 May 2017|work=Times of India|date=26 May 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170807060336/http://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/sports/football/top-stories/bengaluru-fc-submit-bid-as-itb-submission-deadline-ends/articleshow/58851199.cms|archive-date=7 August 2017|url-status=live}} It was also announced that [[Bengaluru FC|Bengaluru]], the two-time champion of the [[I-League]], India's top-tier professional [[association football|football]] league, had submitted a bid.
